changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7298-discussion-explicit-composition.md`

- names `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md` → `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md` — edited by this change

  > Docs: `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md`.

### `.changeset/8067-component-input-member-kind.md`

- names `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` → `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > A registration's `type: 'array'` said a value was a list and stopped there, so a member that drifted from `@objectstack/spec` was invisible to every layer that reads a declaration. `page:header.actions` is the measured cost: the contract declares `z.array(z.string())` ("Action IDs"), the renderer read the members as `ActionDef` objects, and the repo-wide parity gate in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` stayed green for the whole life of the drift because both sides carried the key and neither could say what was inside it. What settled it was a maintainer ruling, not a test — and even after the fix, "these are ids" survived only as English in the registration's `description`.

### `.changeset/8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md`

- names `record-related-list.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

### `.changeset/9964-related-list-picker-filter-mirror.md`

- names `record-related-list.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — edited by this change

  > So one key carried two declarations, with the looser one on the face an author — or an AI writing metadata — reads: `unknown` offers no shape guidance for a key whose consumer demands a specific shape. Nothing could report the divergence either, because `record-related-list.tsx` reached the block through four `(schema as any).add` reads; a cast unwraps the declaration at its own read site, so no compiler ever compared the two.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `54a78308a` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1837 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2449 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36771596268)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `95a8cd520edaeceaeef5e39007610379312ba69c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#11163 (body, claim `5917731712`, dev report `5919004096`), the ruling record on objectstack#20665 (`5902374623`, batch #247, ENFORCE), PR objectui#11263 (body, 6-file list, net diff at merge base `af9e9572c7`), the check-runs on the head, and the spec source at objectstack `0f6dcac5e9` (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, `actions: z.array(z.string()).optional()`, "Action IDs available for related records").

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — unchanged, right.** The spec key is untouched (the ruling keeps it declared). The registration's `inputs` already carried `{ name: 'actions', type: 'array', of: 'string', description: 'Action IDs available for related records' }` (`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:648`) and `RecordRelatedListComponentProps.actions?: string[]` (`packages/types/src/record-components.ts:473`); neither file is in the diff. Nothing an author could write before is refused at parse now.

**Public surface — `record:related_list` honours a published key it ignored, right, and the composition rule is stated and pinned.**
- Absent: `relatedListActionsNeedLookup(undefined)` is false, so `useMetadataItem('object', null)` is the documented no-op (`AppShellContext.tsx:116-139`, no `getItem` call); `placedActions` is `null`, and `toolbarActions` / `rowActions` fall through to `handlers.toolbarActions` / `handlers.rowActions` — the bridge default byte-for-byte. Pinned by the CONTROL case: registration order `['invite','export_csv']` / `['send_welcome','deactivate']`, no notice, `getItem` never called with `('object','contact')`.
- Authored: `useMetadataItem('object', objectName)` + `resolveDeclaredActionIds(authored, relatedObjectMeta.actions)` — the same pair `record:quick_actions` (`record-quick-actions.tsx:187-192`) and `record:alert` (`record-alert.tsx:266-289`) resolve through, over the same `MetadataProvider`; no second registry. Placement is `actionRendersAt(action, 'list_toolbar' | 'list_item')`, the one predicate the bridge's own `deriveActions` applies (`RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx:187-200`). The authored list REPLACES the default (a subset drops the unnamed toolbar action — pinned), renders in authored order on both surfaces from one list (pinned against a registry whose order differs from every authored case), and runs through the bridge's executor with the resolved, localized def (pinned: `onToolbarAction` receives `{ name: 'invite', label: 'Invite', type: 'api' }`).
- `[]`: `classifyDeclaredActions([])` is the empty `objects` arm (`ui-action.ts:210`), so no lookup, nothing placed, nothing refused; built-in New stays because it is not an action id. Pinned (`related-list-new` present, no toolbar, no row menu, no notice).
- Only the ids arm is accepted; the inline-object arm (`page:header`'s transition tolerance) is refused whole. Right for this key's `z.array(z.string())` contract.

**Loud refusal — author-visible, never a silently dropped button. Right.** `describeRelatedListActionRefusals` names each unresolved id ("is not an action of X", or "could not be resolved: no metadata for X was found" when the object itself never arrived), each unplaced id (naming both `list_item` and `list_toolbar`), and a non-array / inline-object / mixed array (`kind: 'array'`), in one `role="status"` `aria-live="polite"` notice beside the list. The in-flight guard (`needsActionLookup && relatedObjectMetaLoading` → nothing drawn, nothing refused) is sound because `useMetadataItem` starts at `loading: !!name`, so the first paint is guarded; the resolvable entries still render because `toolbar` / `row` are populated alongside `refused`. Five pins: unresolved id (notice + `role=status` + `['invite']` still drawn), unplaced `header_only`, inline-object array refused whole, in-flight CONTROL, no-host CONTROL (the refusal is the registry's, not the host's). One branch is code-only: a bare non-array value hits the first guard in `placeAuthoredRelatedListActions` with no pin; the registration declares `type: 'array'`, so this is defence in depth, not a gap.

**Parity ledger — right, and the 5 → 4 account verified against main.** At merge base `af9e9572c7`, `MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTIONS` held the four `owedEntries` units (`element:definition-list.items`; `element:repeater.fields`, `.filter`, `.sort`, all owed to objectui#11168 under objectui#11111 decision 3 = B) plus `'record:related_list.actions': NO_READ_SITE_TO_PIN` — five entries, ceiling 5. At head: the four owed entries remain, ceiling 4, the `NO_READ_SITE_TO_PIN` constant is deleted with its one entry (a comment stands where it was, the `AWAITING_A_PIN` pattern), and `MEMBER_PINS['record:related_list.actions']` names the new pin file. The bound is `toBeLessThanOrEqual(MEMBER_PIN_EXEMPTION_CEILING)` plus "no exemption may also be a pin", both satisfied. History of the constant on main: 1 at `fe41dc76a5` (slice 18, 2026-09-29T14:25Z) → 7 at `81f849852a` (objectui#11073, the 17.5.0 bump, 2026-09-30T03:45Z) → 5 at `3cc4fe567b` (objectui#11168 slice 1, 2026-09-30T12:52Z) → 4 here. The card (filed 2026-09-30T01:36Z) wrote "1 → 0" against the pre-bump ledger; the one rise since the objectui#8176 correction is objectui#11073's, a ruling on main before this branch, and this diff only lowers. The dev's deviation is exact.

**Measured, not changed — confirmed.** `RelatedRecordActionsValue.resolve` takes `{ objectName, relationshipField, parentId }` and `deriveActions(childDef, …, location)` is keyed on the child object (`RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx:334-447`): no per-list channel exists, so `actions` is the per-list channel rather than a duplicate. The net diff at merge base is exactly the six files the PR lists; `index.tsx`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx` and `RelatedList.tsx` are not among them.

**Docs (`content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md:153-184`) — match the diff.** Default = child object's `list_toolbar` / `list_item` actions; authored = ids, replaces, authored order; placement by each action's own `locations`; `[]` = none while New / Edit / Delete / open-row follow `userActions` and permissions; unresolved and unplaced ids named in a notice. The `json` example is a valid node. The inline-object refusal is not described; the heading says the key "holds IDS", so that is an omission of a refusal branch, not a wrong statement. Sits beside the file's existing related-list paragraphs (`limit`, `columns`).

**Check-runs on the head, at review time:** 32 success (Type Check, Lint, Build & E2E, Test (dist pins), the five Changeset gates, every doc gate, Line Citation Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec-free gates), 3 skipped (coverage ×2, dependabot), and 7 `in_progress` — **not concluded**: Spec Main Shape Gate, Test (shard 1/8), Test (shard 2/8), Test (shard 3/8), Test (shard 5/8), Test (shard 7/8), Test (shard 8/8). Shards 4/8 and 6/8 are success. No failure on the head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11163-related-list-actions.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': minor`. Right. `@object-ui/plugin-detail` is the only published package whose source changes (`apps/console` is the private ledger app; `content/docs` is docs). `Clause-②: yes` is on the claim and at the head of the PR body, and it is the right word: a published block starts honouring a declared key, which widens what an author can effect through the public face; `yes` takes at least `minor` (objectstack AGENTS.md, the Clause-② rule), and no `(narrowing)` arm applies because the spec, the registration and the types are untouched and nothing previously accepted is refused at parse. The render-time change for pages that already author `actions` is the ruling's stated consequence ("today an authored `actions` silently does nothing; enforced, it renders") and the changeset carries it under ⚠️ in the text that ships to `CHANGELOG.md`. The changeset body's claims (same lookup as `record:quick_actions.actionNames`, placement by `locations`, `[]` = none, the three refusal reasons, no extra request when absent) each correspond to code in the diff. Changeset Bump Policy, Declaration, Claim Re-read, Fixed Group Check and Overwrite Report: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
1. Ceiling 5 → 4, not 1 → 0 — verified above against `fe41dc76a5` / `81f849852a` / `3cc4fe567b`; accepted.
2. `slotted-pages.md` outside the claim's file list — docs-driven addition, accurate to the diff; the `plugin-detail` README left to PR objectui#11246's surface. Accepted.
3. New module `relatedListActions.ts` beside the renderer — pure resolve-and-place, imported by the renderer only; keeps the renderer exporting components. Accepted.
4. Merged `main` at `af9e9572c7` into the branch — the net diff at that merge base is the six files; nothing else rides. Accepted.
5. Commit trailer form — not a contract matter. Noted.
6. Bridge, `RelatedList.tsx`, `index.tsx` untouched — confirmed in ①.

`open_questions`: none.

Out-of-scope findings, judged:
- **objectstack's `action-name-undefined` lint does not walk `record:related_list.actions`** (`packages/lint/src/validate-action-name-refs.ts:27-30`, "`actions` is declared separately on `record:related_list`"). That exclusion was written when the key was dead; from this head the key is an action-id reference list exactly like `record:quick_actions.actionNames`, so a misspelled id is refused only at runtime. Public-door, objectstack-side, reach = every page authoring the key. **Fileable**: the seat should file it on objectstack (or bind it to the card that closes objectstack#20665 as a filed item, not a note). Not blocking here.
- **`record_related` location** — a declared-not-honoured gap on the LOCATION, not on this key. `record:related_list.actions` carries no location semantics and this PR honours it. But the reach is measured and real: objectstack `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts:215` (`showcase_log_time`, `locations: ['record_header', 'record_related', 'record_section']`), `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json:1523` ("record_related — showcase_log_time on the related-list section"), `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx:276` ("Related-list sections") and `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx:269`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:1163`; in objectui there is no read of `record_related` in any source, test, example or doc.
